patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing left leg pain progressively getting worse over 2 months, now interfering with sleep. Symptoms did not improve with ibuprofen. Noted trauma to the leg with a baseball hit one week before the onset of symptoms, which caused redness and swelling.

Secondary_Symptoms: History of trauma to the leg

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history. First episode of such symptoms.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: The patient is a middle school student. No relevant social history.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, weight loss, or any recent illnesses.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive left leg pain.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “I’m a 13-year-old boy. For the past two months I’ve had steadily worsening pain in my left leg, and it’s now bad enough that it keeps me from sleeping. About a week before it started, a baseball hit my leg and I had redness and swelling, and ibuprofen hasn’t helped.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “I’ve had noticeable swelling right where the baseball hit my left leg, but I don’t think I’ve had swelling in other joints.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on my scalp. It’s mainly been the pain, redness, and swelling where the baseball hit my left leg.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a sensation of itchiness lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had itching or a sensation of itchiness anywhere on my skin—just the pain and redness/swelling in my left leg where the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble raising your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have trouble raising my arms above my head—my main issue has been the worsening pain, redness, and swelling in my left leg.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any loss of vision at all—no vision changes, with or without pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever like that—I haven’t felt extremely hot, dizzy, or had any very high temperature. It’s mainly been the progressive left leg pain with the redness and swelling where the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t been unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately—my main problem has been the worsening pain and the redness and swelling in my left leg after the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills. I’ve mainly just had the steadily worsening pain in my left leg with the redness and swelling where the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses anywhere on my chest or breasts—nothing that feels fixed or doesn’t move. My concern has been just the worsening pain, redness, and swelling in my left leg after the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t felt any pain or discomfort on my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips—it's mostly all focused on my left leg where the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does that pain go away when you stop walking?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: “Yes—when I walk, my left calf hurts more, and it doesn’t really feel better right away when I stop; the pain stays there and has been getting worse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual—it seems about the same as always. My main issue is still the worsening left leg pain with the redness and swelling after the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it hard to lift your arm above your head or reach across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “I don’t have any trouble lifting my arm above my head or reaching across my body—my symptoms are all in my left leg, where it’s been getting more painful with redness and swelling after the baseball hit.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that using the same joints repeatedly—like typing, playing an instrument, or doing repetitive sports—often leads to discomfort or pain?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed that repetitive use like typing or sports makes it worse—my pain seems mainly tied to my left leg and started after the baseball hit. It’s been steadily getting worse over the last two months and isn’t improving with ibuprofen.”
